 Katie & Nathaniel — Behind the Scenes  2007-07-18

Alternate 'What If' Dossier (Ending C — 6:40 AM): Sneaking Past the Morning Janitor—And Rolling Out Into Their Own Missing-Persons Command Post

What Happens When the Night Supervisor Lies Over Heather's 10:44 PM Text, Nate and Katie Pull Off a Flawless Dawn Stealth Exit, & They Ask Their Own Search Party Who Went Missing

Episode 7, Chapter 2, Part 2: Caught Sleeping Together in a Closet ↗ Katie & Nathaniel (27 Dossiers) Copy Link: Read on Phone

Scan with your camera to continue reading this dossier on your phone or tablet.
Story Date & Time 2007-07-18 • 01:10–08:45 EDT
Setting Campus Recreation Hall & Main Quadrangle, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center, Fishersville, Virginia
Archival Source RaggieSoft Backstage Production Dossier
Addressed To Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 7, Chapter 2, Part 2)

Archival Note: In Alternate 'What If' — Ending A (1:35 AM), angry Wesley refuses to wait for grown-ups and yanks the locked Rec Hall door open himself two hours before David Prairie arrives; in Ending B (3:50 AM), Heather and Wesley wait out RRC's bureaucratic stubbornness until David finishes his two-and-a-half-hour drive from Alexandria at 3:45 AM and asks whether anyone actually flipped the closet light switch on.

In Ending C (6:40 AM), one bureaucratic lie tips the night even further into pure comedy gold: to save his own skin after falsifying the 1:00 AM state incident form, the Night Supervisor swears up and down—first to Heather at 1:20 AM, and again to David and the Augusta County Sheriff's Office at 3:45 AM—that he personally entered the Rec Hall seasonal closet with a high-beam flashlight and checked behind every coat rack and curtain, insisting Nate's 10:44 PM text was a decoy, keeping everyone out of the Rec Hall until dawn, and setting up the greatest accidental stealth exit in Fishersville history.

1. 1:10 AM – 6:20 AM — Nine Minutes From Waynesboro, 2.5 Hours From Alexandria, & A Signed Lie on the Hood

Just as in Ending A and Ending B, right before powering both of their flip phones completely OFF inside the unlocked Rec Hall seasonal storage closet at 10:44 PM Tuesday night, Nate sent an <sms> message to Heather Collins: telling her that a classmate had hit Katie's nose in the pool, giving their exact location (the seasonal storage closet at the end of the back hallway in the Rec Hall), letting her know both phones were being shut completely off for the night, and promising that if this didn't work out tonight, tomorrow they would sleep at the hotel with her and Wesley—comfortable telling Heather they were hiding in a closet because she already knew they slept in their bedroom closet at home (while RRC's Level 2 Overnight Pass rules required advance counselor approval plus pickup by a Parent or Legal Guardian, ruling Heather out that evening).

When the 9:30 PM Shenandoah Valley Transit (SVT) Route 250 Connector check-in logs and the 11:00 PM Barton Hall curfew check both come up empty, Dr. Evelyn Cross wakes both Priority Emergency Contact #1 Heather Collins (staying near the Waynesboro ValueMart, roughly seven miles / eight to ten minutes away) and Parent David Prairie (in Alexandria, roughly 155 miles / two hours and thirty minutes away via I-66 West, I-81 South, and I-64 East Exit 91) at 1:10 AM:

  • 1:20 AM — Heather & Wesley Arrive in Nine Minutes (More Than Two Hours Ahead of David):
    Reading Nate's 10:44 PM text the instant she flips open her phone in Room 114, Heather calms Wesley right away ("They aren't lost, Wes—Nate texted me they're sleeping in the Rec Hall closet just like their closet at home with their phones turned off!"), calls David on his cell as he merges onto I-66 West so he knows the twins aren't hurt on the highway (while furious over Katie's unnotified pool injury, David stays on I-66 and I-81 for the full two-and-a-half-hour drive!), and pulls her silver accessible van onto the RRC campus with Wesley at 1:20 AM—just nine minutes after her phone rang.
  • 1:20 AM & 3:45 AM — The Night Supervisor's Career-Ending Double-Down:
    When Heather walks into Barton Hall at 1:20 AM—and again two hours and twenty-five minutes later at 3:45 AM when David Prairie finally pulls in from Alexandria—showing Augusta County Sheriff's Sergeant Holloway and Dr. Cross Nate's 10:44 PM text naming the Rec Hall seasonal storage closet, the Night Supervisor breaks into a cold sweat. On the 1:00 AM Missing Vulnerable Adult Incident Sheet already faxed to Richmond, he signed his legal signature certifying that he "personally entered the Rec Hall seasonal storage closet with a flashlight at 23:26, checked behind every coat rack and stage curtain, and verified the room 100% empty."
    Terrified of admitting in front of two police agencies, a furious parent, and his Director that he lied on a state affidavit without ever flipping the light switch on, the Night Supervisor doubles down at full volume—insisting that Nate must have sent that 10:44 PM text as a decoy before slipping off campus!
  • 3:50 AM – 6:20 AM — Searching Route 250 While Heather, Wesley, & David Wait for Dawn:
    Forced by the signed state affidavit to clear off-campus corridors too, Sheriff's deputies and Virginia State Police troopers check U.S. Route 250 between Staunton and Waynesboro, the emergency-room triage desk across the highway, and the I-81 / I-64 interchanges until 6:20 AM, when warm golden July sunrise crests the green Blue Ridge Mountains and the cruisers regroup on the curved brick turnaround of the main RRC quadrangle beside David's pickup and Heather's accessible van. Having waited on campus since 1:20 AM with Wesley while David joined them at 3:45 AM, Heather crosses her arms and repeats calmly: "Mr. Prairie, Nate does not send decoy texts. The minute somebody unlocks that Rec Hall for the morning shift, they're sitting behind those curtains."

Sixty yards behind them, tucked cozily behind racks of winter coats and heavy burgundy velvet stage curtains inside the air-conditioned Rec Hall seasonal storage closet, Katie and Nate Prairie wake up after eight uninterrupted hours of the best sleep they have had since leaving Virginia Beach.

2. 6:22 AM – 6:39 AM — Operation Speed-One Stealth Inside the Rec Hall

Stretching his shoulders in the quiet dark without hitting a single dorm wall, Nate checks his watch (6:22 AM—both of their powered-off flip phones are still zipped inside their pockets so they won't chime inside the building!) and grins across at Katie in the faint grey crack of light beneath the unlocked wooden door.

"Katie," Nate whispers, barely believing their luck, "nobody opened the door all night! We actually pulled it off!"

Before Katie can whisper back, the heavy steel side maintenance door down by the vending machines clanks open. Footsteps shuffle across the waxed game-room tile, accompanied by the rhythmic squeak-rattle of a yellow wheeled mop bucket and a portable transistor radio softly playing early-morning Shenandoah country music as Earl, the 6:25 AM weekday custodian, props the front glass vestibule latches unlocked for morning air and starts mopping around the billiard tables.

Katie's blue eyes light up past the white medical gauze strip taped across the bridge of her nose.

"Nate, listen to me," Katie breathes into his ear, thinking purely about outsmarting a Barton Hall curfew clipboard. "Barton Hall knows we weren't in our beds at eleven o'clock, right? Right now they probably think somebody in Cantor Hall hid us, or they have zero proof where we went! Nobody saw us roll in here last night—so if we sneak out of this building right now without Earl or a single staffer laying eyes on us, nobody at RRC will ever figure out our unlocked-closet trick! We can power our phones on outside, text Heather good morning, and roll straight into the six-forty-five breakfast line like nothing happened!"

Nate grins from ear to ear and gives her a silent thumbs-up. Operation Speed-One Stealth is on:

  1. 6:26 AM — Erasing Every Trace Inside the Closet:
    Moving in slow motion so not a zipper clicks, Katie and Nate stand up in their sneakers, fold the heavy burgundy stage curtain along its exact original creases, slide it silently onto the middle steel shelf, and fluff the two canvas winter-coat bags back into line.
  2. 6:30 AM — Unfolding Two Wheelchairs Without a Single Squeak:
    Lifting their two collapsed black cross-brace manual wheelchairs out from behind the coat racks an inch at a time, Nate holds both thumbs over the steel seat-rail joints while pressing down gently so the frames lock open without their usual metallic clack. Wrapping their fleece hoodie cuffs around the plastic battery latches to muffle the snap, both twins slide their 24-volt battery boxes underneath, transfer smoothly into their seats, click their power toggles on, and turn their right-armrest speed dials all the way counterclockwise to Setting 1—slowing their electric hub motors to a near-silent crawl.
  3. 6:34 AM — Timing the Mop Bucket:
    Easing the unlocked closet door open two inches, Nate peeks down the darkened rear corridor toward the sunlit main game room. Twenty feet past the billiard tables, Earl whistles along to his radio, pushes his yellow mop bucket through the propped-open door of the men's restroom, and turns the utility sink faucet on full blast.
  4. 6:36 AM — Behind the Ping-Pong Tables & Freezing at the Trophy Case:
    Nate waves two fingers behind his back. Rolling nose-to-tail at two miles per hour in utter silence, Nate and Katie glide out of the rear corridor, tuck low behind the green folded tops of three tournament ping-pong tables so their heads stay below sightline, and reach the tall oak-and-glass trophy case beside the front vestibule—just as the utility faucet shuts off and Earl steps halfway back to the restroom doorway to grab a roll of brown paper towels off his cart!
    Directly behind the five-foot wooden trophy cabinet, both twins take their fingers completely off their joysticks and don't breathe for six heart-pounding seconds until Earl disappears back inside the tiled restroom humming to the chorus.
  5. 6:39 AM — Slipping Out the Front Vestibule Unseen:
    Pressing the rubber bumper of his front footrest gently against the horizontal brass push-bar of the propped vestibule door so the latch doesn't click, Nate holds the glass door wide for Katie's wheels, follows her smoothly onto the shaded concrete porch, and glides silently down the side brick ramp behind the tall, trimmed green boxwood hedge separating the Rec Hall from the main campus quadrangle.

Not a single soul inside the Recreation Hall ever saw them enter, sleep, or leave.

3. 6:40 AM — Rounding the Boxwood Hedge Into Dad, Heather, Wesley, & Two Police Agencies

"Zero witnesses," Nate whispers triumphantly as they roll down the brick path behind the boxwood hedge, dialing his speed knob back up to normal cruising speed while Katie suppresses a proud giggle beside him. "Let's see our counselor prove where we—"

Nate's words die in his throat as both wheelchairs glide side by side past the end of the green boxwood hedge into the warm golden 6:40 AM July sunlight of the main campus quadrangle.

Katie and Nate pull back on their joysticks at the exact same instant, stopping dead on the bricks.

Parked bumper to bumper around the circular brick turnaround between Barton Hall and the Dining Hall—blue roof lightbars pulsing silently against the red-brick walls in the summer dawn—sit three Augusta County Sheriff's cruisers, two grey-and-blue Virginia State Police cruisers, and two RRC Campus Police sedans. Gathered around a campus map taped across a cruiser hood stand half a dozen uniformed deputies and troopers, a pale, hollow-eyed Dr. Evelyn Cross, a clipboard-clutching Night Supervisor with dark circles under his eyes—and, twenty feet to the right beside Dad's pickup truck and Heather's silver accessible van, their father David Prairie holding a foam coffee cup right alongside Heather Collins and Wesley!

Having spent the last twenty minutes sneaking past a janitor with their phones still powered off so they wouldn't get a petty curfew slip, neither Katie nor Nate has even a microscopic suspicion that this entire law-enforcement task force is here for them.

"Whoa, Nate," Katie whispers in wide-eyed shock, staring at the police cruisers and the map on the hood. "Somebody must have escaped off campus in the middle of the night! Wait—is that Dad's pickup truck AND Heather's van?!"

"What on earth are Dad, Heather, and Wes doing on campus at six-forty on a Wednesday morning?!" Nate whispers back, completely mystified.

Rolling casually out across the sunny brick courtyard right behind the semicircle of troopers—looking around the Barton Hall lawn with genuine neighborly curiosity to see what the commotion is about—Nate raises his voice cheerfully over the quiet murmur of police radios:

"Dad?! Heather?! Wes?! What are all of you doing here at six-forty in the morning—and who went missing?!"

Fourteen heads whip around 180 degrees at the exact same millisecond.

For four full seconds of absolute, pin-drop Shenandoah Valley silence:

  • David Prairie's jaw drops open so fast he nearly drops his foam cup of black coffee straight onto his shoes.
  • Heather points straight from the twins to her flip phone to the Night Supervisor without even needing to say "I told you so," while Wesley breaks into a huge grin beside her.
  • Dr. Evelyn Cross grabs the edge of the cruiser fender as if two ghosts just materialized out of the boxwood bushes.
  • The Night Supervisor—whose signed state certification swearing that he personally checked behind every coat rack and stage curtain in the Rec Hall seasonal closet with a flashlight is literally sitting under the Sheriff's Sergeant's elbow on the hood—turns the exact shade of a boiled lobster.
  • And Augusta County Sheriff's Sergeant Holloway slowly lowers his grease pencil, stares once at Heather's phone, stares once at the Night Supervisor, stares through the glass doors of the Rec Hall fifty feet behind the twins where Earl is still happily mopping the lobby oblivious to the universe, and looks back at Katie and Nate sitting side by side in clean hoodies and jeans.

"Who went missing?!" Sergeant Holloway repeats, fighting for his life not to burst out laughing in front of two State Troopers. "Son, half of Augusta County, the Virginia State Police, and your family have been up since one o'clock this morning looking for THE TWO OF YOU—even after Heather showed us your text message naming that exact closet, because somebody signed a state form swearing he checked behind every curtain in there with a flashlight!"

Katie and Nate blink in unison, look at each other across their armrests, look at David, Heather, and Wesley striding across the bricks to wrap both of them in hugs and happy knuckle-taps, and look straight at the crimson-faced Night Supervisor.

"Looking for us?!" Katie blurts out in total, innocent astonishment, pointing her thumb back over her shoulder toward the Rec Hall behind the hedge. "We didn't leave campus! We were sixty yards right over there asleep behind the stage curtains in the seasonal closet—exact place Nate texted Heather! We only left the door unlocked—didn't anybody turn the light switch on?!"

Watching Sergeant Holloway slowly turn his head back toward the Night Supervisor—"Checked behind every coat rack and curtain at 23:26, huh?"—while Dr. Evelyn Cross closes her eyes in pure career-ending agony is a sight neither Katie, Nate, Heather, Wesley, nor David ever forgets for the rest of their lives.

4. 7:00 AM – 8:45 AM — Criminal Handcuffs for Chris, Tina's Thumb Drive, & Leaving Fishersville Together

Just like in Ending A and Ending B, having the Augusta County Sheriff's Office and Virginia State Police standing ten feet away when David and Heather examine Katie's bandaged, bruised nose shatters RRC's ability to sweep Tuesday afternoon's pool assault under the rug:

  • 7:15 AM — Arresting Christopher Vance (Saving Natalie Twelve Hours Early): Learning right on the courtyard bricks that Christopher Vance struck Katie across the face and ripped her swimsuit top in the therapeutic pool yesterday afternoon—and that nobody at RRC called the police or notified her father until they thought she had vanished—David files an immediate criminal assault-and-battery complaint with Sergeant Holloway. Deputies walk straight into Barton Hall and take Christopher Vance out in handcuffs before breakfast finishes—preventing Wednesday night's dorm-database keycard attack on cognitively disabled classmate Natalie before it can ever happen!
  • 8:30 AM — Packing Up With a Full Night's Sleep & Tina's PHP / SQL Drive: While half of Barton Hall cheers quietly from the second-story windows watching David hoist Katie's and Nate's folded wheelchairs beneath the camper shell of his pickup (Day 11) right beside Heather and Wesley's van, classmate Tina walks briskly out of the Dining Hall breezeway, adjusts her glasses with a grin of pure admiration at the twins who defeated state bureaucracy with an unlocked doorknob, a 10:44 PM text to Heather, and Speed Setting 1, and slips a 2-gigabyte USB drive packed with the rest of Mr. Alderman's Web Applications Developer PHP and SQL modules straight into Nate's hand before the whole family rolls out of Fishersville free.
